comments.author: EffectNo2152
comments.body: Youre doing what I would do if I had a better GPU.  Vibe coding a Mini game studio and engine, then build.

replies.author: Maximum-Substance-62
replies.body: I'm not exactly launching rockets, either. Lol. I've got a 16G radeon rx 7800. I have been very pleasantly surprised at the models I get with trellis 2 running locally. Ofc, they don't compare to meshy 7

replies.author: 12OffIntx
replies.body: I was fortunate enough to get a 4090 back before everything went crazy. I've got ComfyUI set up with several model options, including ones carefully chosen as to allow for commercial viability. I have a rule to try local first, let me judge, then go platform (OpenAI Image 2.5) if needed. Its working pretty well. My specific need is for plates and not 3D animation under my current direction.

comments.author: Financial-Metal-7702
comments.body: How are you currently handling rigging and animation? I’m developing an action combat game as a solo dev, and since it features a wide variety of monsters, I'm looking for AI-powered tools or automated pipelines to help streamline the process. Any recommendations?

replies.author: Maximum-Substance-62
replies.body: So far I have used Maximo for auto rigging my enemies for rudimentary animations and I'm using a free asset from the unity store as my main player avatar. It comes fully rigged and it deforms very nicely
